notes:
I've written verse-by-verse notes on Hosea 9 below, but parts 2 and 3 are thin. I found no Lutheran, Pentecostal, Catholic or Orthodox material on this chapter. I didn't use netbible.org's own notes or bibleodyssey.org (I only saw the NET translation through other sites), and I found nothing on prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace readings. The traditional reading (part 1) is well covered. The commentators split mainly over how to read particular verses, not along denominational lines. Where a teacher's tradition is known, I've noted it.

**v. 1**
- The joy probably reflects a harvest festival, a time of Baal worship. Hosea commands Israel to stop celebrating, because good harvests hid a turning away from God. "Like the nations" stings because Israel was chosen to be different from the pagans but now worshipped like them. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary and https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Guzik, citing Boice: Hosea probably preached this at a harvest festival. Israel worshipped idols on threshing floors believing it helped the harvest, so God would curse the harvest. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
- Matthew Henry: people who are stingy toward God are often lavish on their own desires. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Utley thinks it is very hard to tell whether "harlots' earnings" is literal or figurative. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9

**v. 2**
- The point is that the LORD, not Baal, was the source of fertility. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Lloyd Ogilvie: The deception of prosperity among the people to whom Hosea spoke would soon be exposed. The threat of losing food and wine in their threshing floors and winepresses is explained in Hos 9:3. The people will not enjoy the produce of the land because they will no longer dwell there. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary

**v. 3**
- Ogilvie sees Israel's history being reversed: they go back toward the bondage of the Exodus. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Keil and Delitzsch: Egypt is simply as a type of the land of captivity, so that Assyria is represented as a new Egypt. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-4.htm
- Coffman likewise thinks no actual exile in Egypt is contemplated. — https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/hosea-9.html
- Utley: Egypt probably stands for slavery, though some scholars see a political alliance (King Hoshea appealed to Egypt). Assyria means the 722 BC exile. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Unclean food: in exile they would be reduced by necessity to eat meats pronounced unclean by the Mosaic law (Ezekiel 4:13) (Jamieson-Fausset-Brown). — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfu/hosea-9.html

**v. 4**
- "Bread of mourners": food eaten around a death was ceremonially unclean (Numbers 19:14; Deuteronomy 26:14). Clarke: By the law, a dead body, and every thing that related to it, the house where it lay, and the persons who touched it, were all polluted and unclean. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-4.html
- Barnes: their sacrifices, if offered as God did not command, would defile, not atone. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-4.htm
- Calvin: God would bar the ungodly from his presence even when their offerings glitter before men. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-4.html
- Coffman: in exile, slave-masters would feed them just to keep them working, with no regard for clean or unclean food. — https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/hosea-9.html
- Translation note: Ellicott notes Kuenen's proposed change to the Hebrew. He also observes that Hosea did not consider the worship of the Northern Kingdom as in itself illegal. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-4.htm

**v. 5**
- A question meant to jolt them awake: their worship was about to be disrupted and the people deported. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Others restrict chag to the Feast of Tabernacles, or harvest festival, the most joyous of them all. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-4.htm

**v. 6**
- Memphis was capital of Lower Egypt and a huge burial site. Utley gives two readings: exiles die in large numbers in slavery, or those who flee to Egypt die there. "Treasures of silver" may mean idols, rich houses, or vineyards. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Matthew Henry: they will find graves in Egypt, as their murmuring ancestors said (Exodus 14:11). — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-4.html
- G. A. Smith: Memphis was chosen as Israel's grave because her vaults and sepulchres were countless and spacious. — https://ccel.org/ccel/smith_ga/expositorprophets1/expositorprophets1.vi.vi.iii.html

**v. 7 (the main point of disagreement)**
Who is called a fool and insane?
- **The people mocking Hosea.** Guzik: the people said this about Hosea for preaching judgment in good times. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/ Utley: they were linking him with the earlier ecstatic prophet bands to ridicule him. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9 Vandermey and Dearman note both readings. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary Some Jewish commentators take the same line: Aben Ezra, Ewald, and many others understand the prophet and spiritual man to mean true prophets, which the people called fools and madmen. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-7.html
- **False prophets exposed by events.**
  - Methodist: Wesley glosses it as The false prophet. The spiritual man — That pretends to be full of the spirit of prophecy. Clarke reads it the same way. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-7.html
  - Reformed: Calvin says the flatterers who hide sins are mad. — same URL
  - Presbyterian: Barnes says The true prophet gives to the false the title which they claimed for themselves. — same URL
  - Pulpit and Kimchi read it this way too. — https://biblehub.com/hosea/9-7.htm
- **Gill (Baptist) combines both:** the true spiritual man was counted mad, but events would show the pretenders were the fools. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-7.html
- **Against the false-prophet view:** the Cambridge Bible argues a false prophet would never be called a 'man of the spirit'. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-7.htm

**v. 8**
- Utley calls the Hebrew very ambiguous and gives three theories: Ephraim was meant to be God's representative; Ephraim was persecuting God's prophet; or Ephraim followed false prophets. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9
- Feinberg: Ephraim was meant to be a watchman for the nations but became a snare instead. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Keil and Delitzsch render it A spy is Ephraim with my God: the prophet a snare of the bird-catcher in all his ways. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-7.htm

**v. 9**
- Gibeah means the horrors of Judges 19. Hosea says Israel in his day is just as bad. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
- Utley: in Hebrew, "gone deep" and "corrupted" work together as one idea, "deeply corrupted." The same word for corruption is used of the golden calf. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9

**v. 10**
- Grapes in the wilderness and early figs are unexpected delights: God remembers Israel's early faithfulness. Baal Peor refers to Numbers 25. People become like the god they love. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
- A "love at first sight" picture, repaid with love for a god of their own making. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary

**vv. 11–12**
- The name Ephraim means "double fruitfulness." now that glory of populousness was to vanish speedily and entirely (Pulpit). — https://biblehub.com/hosea/9-11.htm
- Barnes: Ephraim had parted with God, his true Glory. Gill notes the "glory" has been read as God, as wealth, or (his own choice) as their many children. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-11.htm
- Dearman: it is God himself, Ephraim's true glory, who is leaving. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Calvin: the judgments come in stages, giving Israel time to repent. — https://ccel.org/ccel/calvin/calcom26/calcom26.xvi.xv.html
- Kidner: they worshipped fertility through Baal's sex rites, and their punishment will be childlessness and war. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary

**v. 13**
- The Hebrew is hard. The RSV follows the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint): "Ephraim's sons… are destined for a prey" (Chisholm). Carroll thinks the standard Hebrew text is as good as any proposed change. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Pulpit: Ephraim was a lovely land in whatever direction one looks towards it, like the famous Tyre, yet its men would die in battle. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-11.htm

**v. 14**
- Guzik: Hosea starts an angry prayer, stops himself, and in the end prays a kind of mercy: fewer children to suffer the coming judgment. He warns zealous believers against becoming bitter toward others. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
- Pulpit calls v. 14 the excited question of the prophet, after which the terrible storm of denunciation sweeps on. — https://biblehub.com/hosea/9-15.htm
- Chisholm thinks Jacob's blessing of "breasts and womb" on Joseph is deliberately reversed here. — https://bible.org/seriespage/hosea-9

**v. 15**
- Why Gilgal: it was once a holy place (circumcision renewed, the first Passover in the land) and later a centre of idolatry (Gill). Saul was made king there (Poole, JFB). — https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/brv/hosea/9-15.html and https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-15.htm
- Benson (Methodist) instead sees an allusion to Achan's sin at Gilgal. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-15.html
- Calvin: corrupt worship at Gilgal angered God more than adultery or plunder. — same URL
- What "hated" means:
  - Constable: This is covenant terminology meaning He opposed them; personal emotion is not the main point. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/9-15.html
  - Coffman (Restoration Movement): God hates no man, yet the rejection is total. — same URL
- "I will love them no more":
  - Gill (Baptist) says this does not mean God's special love and favour the Lord bears to his own people in Christ, which is everlasting and unchangeable, only his general, providential favour, which lasts until Israel's conversion (Romans 11:26). — https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/brv/hosea/9-15.html
  - The Bible Says: God never has nor never will stop loving Israel. — https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/tbs/meaning/hos-9-v15-17.cfm
  - BibleHub's study notes contrast the conditional Mosaic covenant with the new covenant of grace. — https://biblehub.com/study/hosea/9-15.htm
- "My house" may mean the land (Ellicott, linking it to an Assyrian word) or a husband putting out an unfaithful wife (JFB). — https://biblehub.com/hosea/9-15.htm and https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-15.htm
- Gill mentions, and rejects, Grotius's "mystical" link of Gilgal with Golgotha. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/9-15.htm

**v. 16**
- Baal was thought to give fertility. God shows he is the real Lord of the womb. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
- "I will slay": God takes responsibility, though Assyria carries it out. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary

**v. 17**
- Chisholm: "wanderers" is the same Hebrew word as "strayed" in 7:13, so the punishment fits the crime. Kidner: wandering became Israel's reputation, "yet it was not the last word" God had for them. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-9-commentary
- Pulpit: the word pictures birds driven from their nest. — https://biblehub.com/hosea/9-15.htm
- Guzik: this is what the old covenant warned of. Believers now come through a better covenant (Hebrews 8:12). — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
